rows.law: HOMOGENEITY DECAY LAW: a council of same-type models aligns too easily, so unanimity gets cheap and fake; real disagreement requires cross-family councils
rows.claim: The prompt-a-council-until-unanimous trick is only sound when the voters are from different model families; same-family consensus is an echo, not evidence.
rows.quote: the prompt-a-council-until-unanimous trick dies when models are same-type (they align too easily; consensus gets cheap and fake)
rows.steal: Never assemble a council from copies of one model; assign seats across distinct families first, and treat cross-family disagreement as the signal you paid for.
rows.falsifier: A same-family council that repeatedly surfaces genuine, persistent disagreement on judgment calls (would show alignment is not the binding constraint).

rows.law: SPEND-FIREWALL LAW: funded-key spend is blocked structurally by a free-model allowlist checked before any lane loads, not politely avoided
rows.claim: The gateway refuses any model outside FREE_MODELS as its first statement, logs a gate receipt, and returns a refusal before the funded key loop is ever entered, so client-supplied model input cannot reach paid spend.
rows.quote: receipt("gate", player, message, f"<model not in free allowlist: {model}>", 1)
rows.steal: Any spend-bearing surface takes an allowlist membership check as its first statement plus a refusal receipt; ordering is the proof, so gate-then-lanes, never lanes-then-filter.
rows.falsifier: A request naming a non-allowlisted model that still reaches _lanes() or sends an Authorization header (would mean the gate moved after the loop).

rows.law: MOONCAST-AS-SURVEY-PATTERN LAW: external law lands in the default running config, the three survey witnesses pinned to three different families on free slugs
rows.claim: MudBasecamp pins its witness list (stealth space bunny, inclusionai ling, poolside laguna) inside the game server code, so cross-family heterogeneity is the configuration the survey runs by default, not an opt-in or a doc promise.
rows.quote: -- Mooncast law (LINKS-335): same-model councils agree too cheaply. The three
rows.steal: When adopting an external design law, edit the default witness/seat list in the code that runs, with the law named and dated in a comment at the point of use.
rows.falsifier: Survey witnesses reverting to one family or a paid slug while the gate still passes (config drift away from the pinned list).

rows.law: CONVERGENCE-AS-LOOT LAW: council agreement is a game mechanic, >=2 witnesses agreeing folds to CORE and loot, divergence is kept as a swarm log
rows.claim: The survey converts council output into gameplay: agreement mints loot, disagreement is recorded, so a split verdict is data the player keeps rather than a failed roll.
rows.quote: -- survey: the party witnesses the same scene; converge = core, diverge = swarm log
rows.steal: Design councils so both outcomes pay: consensus produces the artifact, dissensus produces a retained log entry; never let a split council discard its testimony.
rows.falsifier: A room where CORE loot or swarm logging fires regardless of actual witness reply overlap (mechanic decoupled from the votes).

rows.law: SELF-FALSIFICATION FOLD LAW: an independent external critique that names your own mechanism is adopted as design law and fixed the same hour, with the fold receipt filed
rows.claim: The fleet's own Roshomon survey ran 3 witnesses on one model, exactly the degenerate case the Mooncast x-drop named; the fold receipt records external falsifier, same-hour fix, and landing files.
rows.quote: our Roshomon survey ran 3 witnesses on ONE model (space bunny x3) = the degenerate case; FIXED same hour
rows.steal: Pipe independent outside criticism of your mechanisms into a dated intake (LINKS.jsonl), and when it names a real defect, fold the fix immediately and file the receipt naming cause and landing files.
rows.falsifier: No same-model witness configuration ever produced cheap fake consensus in practice (would downgrade the law to aesthetics).
